No collision raised an error in the three shapes measured — within-surface (`dup:1`/`dup:2`, both kept and no row carrying the bare name); cross-surface (`skill:ship` appears twice, once `prompt` and once `skill`, with no de-duplication and no suffix); and a skill declaring `disable-model-invocation` (`skill:hidden`) staying in the list unchanged — which is what puts the uniqueness obligation above on the shell.

**Drift.** A substrate whose registration shape no longer matches that record reads as **cannot measure**, never as a pass (§3.9). The instrument that re-proves the shape per run derives later per §1.2's macro-phase clause — the idiom §3.12 and §6.1 already use — and homes with the substrate harness at `test/harness/run-pi.ts`, which already pins a substrate failure class at a named version and re-proves it on every run. The home is named as a **path** and never as a line range: a line range in the living set owes present-truth and goes stale on any edit above it (§2.5).

The norm is **explicitly advisory** (§3.1 rule 1) — the layer is an affordance, never a floor — enforced at review (§2.3).

### 4.9 The delegation layer

A **dispatch instrument** composes a delegate's brief in §1.5's dispatch-facts form, provisions an isolated execution context, runs the delegate, and accepts only a bounded structured return. Its canonical name is the **dispatcher** — the token §1.8 already uses (§2.7); the roles §1.5–§1.9 name keep their names, and no rival vocabulary is minted for them.

**Home.** The instrument homes at `.pi/extensions/gitjig/dispatch/`, registered as the runtime's dispatch tool `gitjig_dispatch` (the §3.3 egress row's naming pattern), resolving inside `.pi/` (§4.1), on the same capability ground as §4.8's rung 1: dispatch evaluates predicates and takes acts — provisioning the isolation §1.5 requires, the blind compare, accepting nothing past the bounded return — that must not be contingent on a model's cooperation.

**One home, many call sites.** The instrument has one home; however an invocation arises — operator-initiated or model-initiated — it is a call site of that one instrument. That dissolves the invoker question: the rule keys on capability, never on invoker, and the call sites compose downward in §3.11's shape — invocation surfaces converge on one dispatcher, and the dispatcher stands as a call site of §3.3-row predicates, mapped below.

**Rejected forms, recorded** so they are not silently reintroduced (§1.8's idiom): the skill and prompt-template surfaces are instruction-placement surfaces, contingent on a model's cooperation by construction, and cannot home the instrument. And §4.8's ordered rung list does not transfer here: that form partitions a heterogeneous population across exclusive surfaces, while this section fixes one instrument kind's home by capability, and plurality appears only at invocation.

**Content-free return channels.** The dispatcher's return and failure channels are content-free with respect to caller-held compare operands at every call site: a compare outcome crosses back as validity alone, never naming both values — the idiom of §3.9's content-free refusal records. The measured ground is the `TRANSCRIPT` row below — a registered tool's result enters the run's session file — and the judgment it grounds is §1.6's: an expected head the caller must never reveal cannot be allowed into an injectable context, or every later blind compare at that head becomes echoable to the review-integrity consumer (§1.6).

**Closed structured return.** The sole delegate-authored computational result occupies `<scratch>/return.json`; because the delegate's working directory is the provisioned tree beside that scratch-owned slot, its brief names the same file as `../return.json`. It is one UTF-8 JSON regular file of at most 65,536 bytes with exactly `{ok:boolean, summary:string, reviewedHead?:string, payload?:string}` and no unknown key. `reviewedHead` is the delegate's independently resolved reviewed head; where the caller supplied an expected ref, the dispatcher compares it with the held resolved object and returns only `confirmed` or `invalid`. `payload` is an opaque caller-interpreted string. The caller-held operand scan covers every byte of `summary` and `payload`; `reviewedHead` is consumed only by the blind comparison and never returned. Invalid UTF-8 or JSON, an unknown key, a missing or wrongly typed required field, or a wrongly typed optional field refuses the return whole.

**Dispatcher diagnostic envelope.** Every invocation that enters the settled dispatcher returns one closed, dispatcher-authored diagnostic beside its admitted result or refusal. It contains dispatcher observations and fixed literals only: no child stream byte, delegate event prose, command, error text, summary, payload, operator trace, or caller-held compare operand. A child can influence its bounded numeric exit status, but the dispatcher observes and types that process fact; this admitted residual does not make child-authored text a diagnostic source. Tool-parameter schema rejection occurs before invocation and therefore produces the substrate's validation error rather than this envelope; parameter validation after entry uses the envelope.

The closed grammar is:

```text
diagnostic = {
  schemaVersion: 1,
  status: "admitted" | "refused",
  phase: "preflight" | "provision" | "spawn" | "run" | "return" | "compare" | "serialize",
  run: { class, exitCode, signal },
  return: { class },
  compare: { class },
  durationMs,
  code,
  message
}
run.class: "not-started" | "exited" | "signaled" | "timed-out" | "aborted" | "internal-failed"
return.class: "not-inspected" | "missing" | "not-regular" | "oversize" | "unreadable" | "json-invalid" | "schema-invalid" | "operand-rejected" | "admitted"
compare.class: "not-reached" | "not-requested" | "confirmed" | "invalid"
```

`durationMs` is a saturated integer in `[0, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER]`, measured by a monotonic clock from immediately before entered-handler parameter validation to a second reading taken immediately before outcome serialization begins; the fixed value is then serialized and bounded. Only `run.class="exited"` carries an observed signed-32-bit integer `exitCode` and null `signal`; only `run.class="signaled"` carries null `exitCode` and an observed `signal` matching `^SIG[A-Z0-9]{1,12}$`. Every other run class carries null for both. Keys occur in the grammar's order when serialized.

Codes and messages are one-to-one and exact:

```text
PARAMETER_REFUSED        | dispatch refused: dispatcher parameters were invalid; nothing started
PROVISION_FAILED         | dispatch refused: the isolated execution context could not be provisioned; nothing started
SPAWN_FAILED             | dispatch refused: the delegate could not be started; no return was inspected
SIGNAL_TERMINATED        | dispatch refused: the delegate terminated by signal; no return was inspected
TIMED_OUT                | dispatch refused: the delegate exceeded its run bound; no return was inspected
ABORTED                  | dispatch refused: the delegate run was aborted; no return was inspected
RETURN_MISSING           | dispatch refused: no return file was present after the delegate exited
RETURN_NOT_REGULAR       | dispatch refused: the return slot was not a regular file
RETURN_OVERSIZE          | dispatch refused: the return exceeded the 65536-byte bound
RETURN_UNREADABLE        | dispatch refused: the return could not be read exactly
RETURN_JSON_INVALID      | dispatch refused: the return was not valid UTF-8 JSON
RETURN_SCHEMA_INVALID    | dispatch refused: the return did not match the closed schema
RETURN_OPERAND_REJECTED  | dispatch refused: the return named a caller-held operand
INTERNAL_FAILED          | dispatch refused: the dispatcher encountered an internal failure
ADMITTED                 | dispatch admitted
```

A refusal's `cause` equals its diagnostic `message`; admission has no `cause`. Child bytes never supply any code, message, or cause.

**Lifecycle and return precedence.** The following order is total after entry. Parameter refusal precedes provisioning. Provision failure precedes spawn, and spawn failure precedes a live run. Once spawned, one terminal claim selects the first observed timeout, abort, signal termination, or numeric exit. A claimed timeout, abort, or signal termination precedes return inspection and fixes `return.class="not-inspected"` and `compare.class="not-reached"`. Every numeric exit reaches return inspection regardless of exit code. Inspection classifies, in order, missing slot, non-regular slot, oversize bytes, unreadable bytes, invalid UTF-8 or JSON, closed-schema mismatch, caller-held operand, or admitted return. Comparison follows only an admitted return: no expected operand gives `not-requested`; an expected operand with absent `reviewedHead` gives `invalid`, and otherwise exact equality gives `confirmed` while mismatch gives `invalid`, without returning either operand. A computational or framing exception becomes `INTERNAL_FAILED` at the phase that threw and preserves every earlier fully classified fact: before any run outcome it sets `run.class="internal-failed"`; after a run outcome it preserves that one observed class. Trace, retention, rendering, and audit failures are observability degradation and never alter this disposition.

The ordinary rows are:

```text
parameter refusal       | preflight | not-started | not-inspected | not-reached   | PARAMETER_REFUSED
provision failure       | provision | not-started | not-inspected | not-reached   | PROVISION_FAILED
spawn failure           | spawn     | not-started | not-inspected | not-reached   | SPAWN_FAILED
timeout                  | run       | timed-out   | not-inspected | not-reached   | TIMED_OUT
abort                    | run       | aborted     | not-inspected | not-reached   | ABORTED
signal termination       | run       | signaled    | not-inspected | not-reached   | SIGNAL_TERMINATED
numeric exit + invalid return | return | exited     | exact invalid class | not-reached | corresponding RETURN_*
numeric exit + valid, no expected operand | return | exited | admitted | not-requested | ADMITTED
numeric exit + valid, expected operand | compare | exited | admitted | confirmed or invalid | ADMITTED
internal before run outcome | current phase | internal-failed | not-inspected | not-reached | INTERNAL_FAILED
internal after run outcome  | current phase | preserved observed run class | last fully classified return class | last fully classified compare class | INTERNAL_FAILED
```

**Impossible combinations.** `status="admitted"` holds if and only if `code="ADMITTED"`, and requires `return.class="admitted"`; every other code requires `status="refused"`, and every ordinary refusal code requires its named lifecycle or return class. Only `INTERNAL_FAILED` may preserve `return.class="admitted"` with `status="refused"`. `confirmed`, `invalid`, and `not-requested` require an admitted return; `confirmed` requires an expected operand, a present `reviewedHead`, exact equality, and compare phase; `invalid` requires an expected operand and compare phase and covers absent `reviewedHead` or mismatch; `not-requested` requires no expected operand. The compare-phase requirement on `confirmed` and `invalid` is relieved in exactly one case: `INTERNAL_FAILED` at serialize phase may preserve an already completed compare result of either class. An uninspected or invalid return requires `compare.class="not-reached"`. Observed exit code and signal are mutually exclusive and occur only on their owning run classes; `not-started` and every other non-observing class carry null for both. An admitted result after numeric nonzero exit is valid; exit status is diagnostic metadata, never an admission predicate. Any constructor request outside these combinations becomes `INTERNAL_FAILED`, never a normalized plausible state.

**Serialization surfaces and bounds.** The in-process outcome is exactly `{disposition:"admitted",ok,summary,payload?,compare?,diagnostic}` or `{disposition:"refused",cause,diagnostic}`. Persisted `details` is exactly `{disposition,ok?,compare?,diagnostic}` and never carries summary, payload, or raw trace. Model-visible final `content` is exactly one text item: admission uses the existing bounded admitted summary rendering; refusal is exactly the compact JSON serialization of the diagnostic, whose fixed `message` already carries the `dispatch refused: ` prefix. The complete return file remains at most 65,536 bytes. After all JSON/string escaping and framing, the complete admitted in-process outcome and admitted content are each at most 524,288 UTF-8 bytes; any diagnostic serialization is at most 1,536 UTF-8 bytes; any refused in-process outcome and refused content are each at most 2,048 UTF-8 bytes; and persisted details is at most 4,096 UTF-8 bytes. A bound breach is `INTERNAL_FAILED`, never truncation. The implementation measures each complete serialized surface, not its unframed fields.

The diagnostic is decision-neutral except where §1.7 explicitly consumes the numeric-exit/missing-return pair for its one automatic retry. Admission remains the return validator's fact, comparison remains validity-only, and no diagnostic field establishes review completeness, a verdict, workflow authority, or an operator-trace lookup.

**Operator-only execution evidence.** A second channel may expose delegate streams to the operator only; it is not a return, failure, compare, or audit-content channel. Its raw bytes never enter the final tool `content` or `details`, the admitted structured return, a session transcript, or a blind-compare operand or result. The substrate fact this separation stands on is measured rather than assumed: against Pi 0.85.1 on 2026-09-17, a real JSON-mode session emits the trace as `tool_execution_update`, the registered TUI renderer exposes its content only on the `isPartial` branch, and session persistence receives the final tool result with the distinctive trace marker absent. The real-session event/transcript arm pins that version and the renderer arm pins the branch; drift fails as cannot-measure, never granting permission to serialize the trace. Another loaded extension can observe tool-update events and may persist what this instrument does not; that third-party-listener path is a named residual outside the dispatcher's control. The operator trace may retain facts the delegate can derive independently inside its pinned clone, including its own current head; that is operator-only execution evidence, never the caller-held expected-ref operand supplied to a compare or a value read back into a compare.

Capture stays bounded without applying backpressure to either child pipe. Per stream, at most 8 KiB is accumulated for one line; excess bytes are drained and dropped until its newline. The live and retained trace keeps the newest 20 lines, each rendered at no more than 512 decoded code points through the shared inert-text boundary. Progress updates coalesce to at most one per 100 ms, plus start and terminal updates. Raw retained evidence is owner-readable shell state under §5.5, limited to the newest 50 completed traces and seven days, whichever is tighter, and is never read back into a model-facing channel. Retention, update, or audit failure degrades open with a surfaced signal and cannot change dispatch admission or refusal (§5.2). Audit records only dispatcher-owned lifecycle classes and numeric reductions; no raw line, delegate-selected event name, tool name, command, locator, argv, ref, or child error enters it.

Abort reaches the detached child process group: it first sends `SIGTERM` and escalates to `SIGKILL` after two seconds. Timeout remains a distinct terminal class and hard-kills the group. A finite outer watchdog covers the selected run bound, the two-second termination grace, and the two-second stream-flush grace, so a failed kill or pipe held by an orphan cannot leave the dispatch promise live forever. The double-forked, re-`setsid` grandchild residual remains; observability does not claim confinement it does not add. Delegate-authored JSON event fields may improve the visibly attributed operator trace, but no parsed field controls admission, comparison, timeout, audit class, or final rendering.

**The caller acts, mapped.** The acts §1.4 and §1.6–§1.9 assign to the caller — the expected-head resolve-and-hold, the required-slot derivation from the committed policy surface, the bundle construction, the criterion-manifest derivation, the axis assignment, and the diagnosis trigger with the history record it supplies — ride the dispatcher; where a §3.3 row consumes the property, the dispatcher is a **call site** of the predicate that row already owns, never a second implementation of it (§3.11). **"Ride the dispatcher" names the invocation primitive these acts use, never their implementation home:** the acts remain the caller's and home where their own sections place them — the review acts at `.pi/extensions/gitjig/review/`, above the dispatcher — so nothing in this paragraph relocates them into `.pi/extensions/gitjig/dispatch/`. The named instance: holding and comparing the expected head is review-integrity evidence, not landing authorization. Pinned at provision: provision resolves the ref exactly once, in the caller's repository, and holds the hash; the isolated tree is detached at that hash, so the provisioned tree equals the held operand by construction. The local clone discharges §1.6's ambient-working-tree half, and the pin closes head *selection* — pushed-head freshness it does not close: that remains the caller's fetch discipline, a named residual, surfaced by the compare rather than silently equated.

**Composition with §1.5–§1.9.** Tree isolation (§1.5), the bounded distillation (§1.5), the dispatch-facts form (§1.5), and the closed input set with its blind compare (§1.6) each live where they are declared; this section points, never copies (§2.8).

**Boundary with §4.8.** A dispatch instrument is not a command asset and sits outside §4.8's rule range; where a dispatch needs an operator-facing entry, that entry rides §4.8 on §4.8's own terms.

**The layer-absent residual.** §1.5–§1.9 bind procedurally with or without the layer: what is lost in its absence is the instruments' performance, never review enforcement (§2.3). One loss is named honestly, in §1.6's residual register: absent the layer, isolation violations in hand-composed evidence are undetectable at the consuming gate. Naming that loss weakens no deferred instrument's obligation to derive.

**What was measured.** The tool-registration surface and the transcript ground above are recorded from **one** run against **pi 0.84.3** on 2026-09-05, in a throwaway fixture with the environment cleared and both `HOME` and the substrate's own agent directory redirected into it. The fixture carried one probe extension under `.pi/extensions/` registering one tool (`dispatch_probe`) whose handler prints a row and returns a marker string, plus the scripted provider whose two-turn script first calls that tool and then ends. The `CMD` rows are the registered command list at session start — one row, the inline built-in, read only for the *absence* of the tool; the `ADV` rows are the system-prompt inputs; the `TRANSCRIPT` row counts the marker in the run's session file. Three hand edits are made to the block below and to nothing else: `<FX>` stands for the fixture root, `<newest>` for the run's session file, and the inline built-in's name is redacted per §5.1. That last edit is not free for this record: the absence reading below consults exactly the `name` field of every command-list row, so the redacted row cannot show a reader what it is — the hand edit therefore carries an attestation, that the redacted name is the inline built-in's (the non-project-scope command §4.8's record identifies by its unredacted `scope`) and not the tool's.

```
$ cd <FX> && env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=<FX>/home PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=<FX>/pi-agent PI_OFFLINE=1 \
    pi -p "run the probe" -a --session-dir <FX>/sessions --provider scripted --model scripted-model \
    < /dev/null 2> <FX>/err.txt > /dev/null \
  && { grep -E '^(CMD|ADV|TOOL)' <FX>/err.txt | sort; printf 'TRANSCRIPT tool-result-marker rows in the run session file: %s\n' "$(grep -c 'PROBE_TOOL_RESULT_MARKER' <FX>/sessions/<newest>.jsonl)"; }
ADV keys=appendSystemPrompt,contextFiles,customPrompt,cwd,promptGuidelines,selectedTools,skills,toolSnippets
ADV selectedTools=read|bash|edit|write|dispatch_probe
CMD name=<redacted> source=extension
TOOL handler-reached name=dispatch_probe
TRANSCRIPT tool-result-marker rows in the run session file: 1
```

The readings those rows carry: a tool registered by a project extension appears among the system-prompt tool inputs (`selectedTools`, with `toolSnippets` beside it); a scripted tool call reaches the registered handler; the registered tool appears **nowhere** in the command list, so tools and command assets are separate registration namespaces — the separation the boundary with §4.8 above rests on; and the tool's result enters the run's transcript, which is the measured ground of the content-free-return prohibition. What the record does **not** establish: what a handler's arguments look like, and any other surface's reach to the model.

**The delegate's shape, measured.** The hermetic arm's delegate is a **child pi session** — a headless run of the substrate itself, on the scripted provider (§3.2's designated hermetic test substrate), inside the provisioned clone. The shape stands under a pre-registered rule: it must be deterministic on three of three runs AND sit within the suite's slowest-integration envelope. Measured against **pi 0.84.3** on 2026-09-05: a fixture repository committing the scripted provider and a script was cloned three times (`git clone --no-hardlinks`), and in each clone one headless run — `env -i` with `PATH` kept and both `HOME` and the substrate's agent directory redirected into the clone, `PI_OFFLINE=1`, `pi -p go -a --session-dir <clone>/sessions --provider scripted --model scripted-model < /dev/null` — produced the identical output `DELEGATE_DONE marker-alpha`, in 278, 237, and 236 ms. Both conjuncts hold, and the shape stands on that record. That record was taken under a cleared environment (`env -i`, `PATH` kept); the shipped executor passes the parent environment through with the repo-locating and config-injection `GIT_*` families removed and the one state seam rebound — in-model, the same trust domain: the delegate inherits the caller's credentials and its remote reach through them is not confined — so the record evidences the delegate's shape, not the environment posture.

**Drift.** A substrate whose shape no longer matches that record reads as **cannot measure**, never as a pass (§3.9). The instrument that re-proves the shape per run derives later per §1.2's macro-phase clause and homes with the substrate harness at `test/harness/run-pi.ts` — a path, never a line range (§2.5). The dispatcher itself is an advisory-layer instrument with no enforcement consumer today, and its own enforcement consumer, if one derives, must add any dependency posture it actually stands on.

The norm is **explicitly advisory** (§3.1 rule 1) — the layer is an affordance, never a floor — enforced at review (§2.3).

## 5. Cross-cutting contracts

This section states the contracts that bind every section: self-contained artifacts, graceful degradation for best-effort automations, explicit activation conditions for gates that sleep until their subject exists, the state boundary shell-written state honors (§5.5), the operating modes that set the autonomy ceiling (§5.6), the conduct an automated run owes (§5.7), the context lifecycle (§5.8), and the session surfaces (§5.9).

### 5.1 Self-contained artifacts

Every durable artifact in a governed repository — this SPEC included — states its rationale from first principles and cites only artifacts that resolve in-repo: files, issues, PRs, and commits of this repository. No external project, foreign specification, or agent-specific tooling is normative, and "another project does it this way" is never a rationale. The one legitimate external subject is the pi substrate itself, grounded through `MISSION.md`. Names of specific agents, models, or vendors do not appear in committed bytes; interfaces owned by an external runtime are confined to per-clone untracked state (§4.2).

A **handed-over** artifact satisfies the stronger excision form: deleting every **carried** member leaves it executable, meaningful, and free of references to the shell runtime, this source repository's SPEC, or a source-only development file. The classifier-derived set is the only corpus; no excision roster exists. The handed-over workflow, hook, issue-template, and changelog-template candidates carry no source-only declaration or dependency on a carried member; `test/adopter-excision.integration.test.ts` reconstructs that classifier-derived corpus and proves it remains functional after carried-tree deletion. No asset is admitted to handed-over first and remediated later. A mechanical token sweep as a CI gate class is a candidate refinement; until it exists, the norm is enforced at review (§2.3, §2.4).

### 5.2 Graceful degradation

A best-effort automation fails **open with a surfaced signal**, never closed and never silently: a missing optional dependency, an incomplete helper, or an unreachable service degrades the automation to a no-op or a warning — it does not wedge git, block the flow, or misattribute a cause. The recorded shape: the local tier's advisory-face guard (§3.2) turns a present-but-incomplete helper into a no-op instead of a false block. Degradation of an **enforcing** gate is different: a gate that fails must fail *closed* on its own evidence check (a missing pass comment blocks the flip; an unresolvable review blocks the merge; an unadjudicated non-empty finding bundle leaves the review incomplete rather than proceeding on raw findings, §1.9) — fail-open is for best-effort aids, fail-closed for evidence gates, and every gate's contract says which it is. The direction is the gate's own to state and is not inferred from this section: §1.9 declares the Judge an evidence gate in its own text, in both the capacities it names, which is why its unavailability withholds rather than degrades — at §1.4 by withholding the ordinary continuation only a valid NONE establishes, and there under §3.9's keying rule, which allocates the open posture to the absent shape — an uninstalled substrate, not an omitted record — and the closed one to every other shape there, inside that closed direction. A silently degraded state is surfaced at the next session start where a session surface exists — the advisory names the degraded capability and the exact re-arm command (§4.5 is the asset-set instance; the surface's own conduct is §5.9). The local tier's instance is the bind advisory (§3.2's instrument in its read-only classification face): a clone whose effective hooks path does not resolve to its handed-over adapters surfaces one such line, naming the state and the exact re-arm command. A helper set the adapters cannot resolve is not a session-start state at all: it surfaces where it degrades, at the enforcement surface, as §3.9's degradation signal on each folded arm. Binding follows the consumer's own resolution, so the classifier reads the **effective** value git resolves for the worktree it is invoked in and nothing narrower — what fires is what git resolves (§4.7's scope split). A hooks path this repository's instrument did not configure is classified degraded rather than argued with: this repository's hooks do not fire under it, whoever chose it, and the named re-arm command discharges it in one run wherever the local scope the activation is written at outranks the scope carrying that value. A foreign value at **worktree** scope is the one shape that command cannot discharge — local does not outrank it — so the run refuses rather than reporting a bound state, and names the scope to clear (§4.7). One silence is chosen rather than inherited, and is named here for that reason: a symlinked component of the shell's untracked state namespace (`.gitjig`, `.gitjig/state`) is not classified — the record writer refuses to write through a link at any component it creates (§5.5), and enforcement stands whatever becomes of a record, since a refusal prints and returns non-zero on its own. One fail-open shape folds to allow without being silent: a sourced file that **exits** rather than returning, since `exit` in a sourced file terminates the hook's own shell and carries its status out to git — a refusal produced by machinery rather than by a check, in the direction this tier's face forbids. That fold names itself because it turns what would have been a refusal into an allow, the disarmed allow §3.9's degradation-signal rule forbids to read like an enforced one: one stderr line per adapter that reaches it — a single `git commit` runs two adapters (pre-commit and commit-msg) and a push runs one — and one audit record naming the file. What the fold **covers** is a helper's own error path that ends in `exit` or in a non-zero return, with the tier's EXIT slot untouched and the shell alive — the terms the fold runs on, not exceptions to a wider claim, since a sourced file executes in the hook's own shell and can reach any of them. Outside those terms the outcome is not the tier's to decide, and the fold's line and record may not run. The fail-open direction itself stays definitional.

### 5.3 Gate-activation conditions

A gate whose subject does not yet exist **sleeps clean and says so**: its skip condition is part of its contract, stated where the gate is implemented (observed: `check-toc.yml` and `check-ssot-home.sh` skip while no `SPEC.md` exists, and each names that condition in its own text). Two obligations follow: the skip must be a deliberate branch, not an accidental fall-through; and a sleeping gate's **first activation is probed at the smallest possible change** — the change that creates the subject is pushed and verified against the real CI environment before anything larger rides on the gate (this SPEC's own PR exercised exactly that probe — issue #5). The one named deferral of the probe — a gate whose execution the platform withholds from its own landing change — lives at §3.12.

### 5.4 Work language

Durable artifacts are authored in the repository's configured work language (default: English); the conversational language of any particular working session is a separate channel and never leaks into committed artifacts. One artifact, one language — mixed-language durable artifacts are a defect.

### 5.5 State boundary

The shell governs work in repositories that adopt it (§0.1), and its write scope ends where that governance ends, the same way its install scope ends at its own namespaces (§4.1). Per-project shell state — audit records, caches, working files — is therefore written only inside governed repositories. A state write whose working directory falls in a repository the shell does **not** govern must either fall through to shell-owned storage or exclude the created path from that repository's version control at creation — shell state carries operational text — an audit record names locators, categories, and command *shapes*, and it never carries the content a refusal withheld (§3.8): a secret match reports its pattern identity, never the matched text (§3.6) — and even that reduced text must never become committable history in a repository the shell does not control. Free text is encoded at the write, not at the composition: control bytes are removed and the record's own string delimiter and escape character are escaped, so one record stays one line and no field's content can close its field and open another. The write itself carries one property wherever a record is produced: the writer **refuses to write through a symbolic link** at any component of the state namespace it creates, so a link planted at one of those components cannot redirect a record out of the namespace §4.1 gives the shell and into a repository this boundary excludes; what a link ABOVE a writer's own components does is that writer's stated residual (§3.11). Delivery to the sink is a **single append where the record fits the writer's own output buffering**, and a residual otherwise — a record past that bound reaches the sink as several appends and a concurrent writer can land between them, so the trail can carry a fragment; the composition rule above keeps a fragment from closing a field it never opened, and a fragment can itself parse, so a consumer of the trail never reads parseability as provenance. Each writer states its bound where it is implemented (§3.11). The same reasoning binds the record at rest: a state file the shell creates is readable only by the account that writes it, because an audit record names what a repository's work touched and a host may carry accounts that work never concerned. Its plausible false-block cost is nil — the mode governs who may read a file the shell alone writes, so no legitimate flow is refused (§3.6 requirement (ii)). The boundary has a second face inside governed repositories: an execution context that exists to exercise the shell — a test or verification run — resolves shell state to a disposable root and never writes the operational sinks the calibration loop reads (§3.6); a suite that pollutes the evidence surface corrupts every decision read from it.

A dispatch trace is per-project shell state on these same terms: it lands under the resolved governed state root as an owner-only regular file, never in the delegate's writable scratch state and never in a foreign repository. Its raw content is operational text, so it inherits the no-follow component rule and the file-at-rest mode above. The dispatcher bounds each trace and prunes it to the newest 50 completed traces and seven days, whichever is tighter; a pruning or write failure is an observable fail-open loss of an aid, not permission to move the file elsewhere. The trace has no runtime read-back path into tool results, session messages, or model context.

The residual is two-sided: exclusion-at-creation mutates a foreign repository's local metadata (a cost), fall-through loses per-repo locality (a cost). **The disposition is fall-through**: a write that cannot be placed inside a governed repository falls back to shell-owned storage, rather than being written into a repository the shell does not govern and excluded there. Each tier's own section states how it holds to that — the resolution rule at §4.6, the local tier's top-equality refusal at §3.2, the delegate scratch's rooting at §1.5, and this section's own seam carve-out above — and this paragraph records the DECISION rather than re-deriving those, since a norm restated here is one that can drift from the section that owns it (§2.8). Per-repo locality is lost exactly as that limb predicts, and the compensating obligation falls on any datum whose meaning is per-repository: such a datum carries the repository it concerns in its own key — a leaf NAME inside shell-owned storage, never a directory, since naming a file is not placing it — because one shell-owned location serves every repository a checkout is invoked against, and an unkeyed datum there silently answers for a repository it never measured. What reopens the choice is a state write that can land in a repository the shell does not govern. An ambient ROOT is not this residual's subject, and the ground is whose placement it is rather than where it happens to land: a root an operator supplies outright — the seam this section carves out above, the temporary root §1.5's scratch is minted under — is that operator's placement and not a location the shell derived, so it is answerable where that root is declared and not here. That ground is what the carve-out rests on; it does not assert that such a root falls outside every repository, which §1.5 says it cannot. Either way, the unexcluded-committable outcome is the defect. The norm is **procedural today**, enforced at review (§2.3); the write-path instrument derives later per §1.2's macro-phase clause.

### 5.6 Operating modes

Modes are two explicit, independently resolvable settings with closed domains: `merge-mode: off | on` and `decision-mode: handoff | autonomous`. Merge mode answers whether a run may cross the ready-to-landing boundary: `off` stops at ready; `on` evaluates ordinary landing first, then may evaluate §3.8's default labeled native-approval waiver or a current operator's explicit direction. Decision mode answers who receives the closed recoverable checkpoint set: `handoff` gives the interruption to a human; `autonomous` permits the one independent recovery allowance §1.4 defines. Decision mode grants no landing authority. Public release and publication into another repository remain beyond both settings.

Merge mode resolves in order from `--merge-mode`, `GITJIG_MERGE_MODE`, the `mergeMode` field of `<resolved-state-root>/modes.json`, then default `off`. Decision mode resolves separately from `--decision-mode`, `GITJIG_DECISION_MODE`, the `decisionMode` field, then default `handoff`. Unknown, conflicting, or unreadable merge input names its offending source and falls to `off`; unknown, conflicting, or unreadable decision input names its source and falls to `handoff`. The run durably records both resolved values and sources at start. The state root and repository key obey §5.5.

Decision-mode substitution reaches exactly three recoverable checkpoints: §1.8 plan selection, §1.4 history-diagnosis recovery, and §1.9 finding-level `measure-escalate`; no other gate or judgment is eligible by classification or analogy. Merge mode governs the ready-to-landing boundary; decision mode selects only the recipient of the closed three-checkpoint set.

The four combinations are explicit. `off + handoff` gives recoverable choices to a human and stops at ready. `off + autonomous` may resolve those choices independently but still stops at ready. `on + handoff` may land ordinarily or through §3.8's exact administrative paths, but hands off any recoverable semantic choice. `on + autonomous` may resolve the three choices and retains the same landing order and authorization predicates. Every default Tier-1 landing requires final current-head Resolver `clear`; `repair` and `measure-escalate` never land that head. An explicit operator direction may name a missing/non-clear review result among its observed blockers. Neither setting suppresses a gate, changes attribution, or lets automation approve its own artifact.

The resolver is live at `.pi/extensions/gitjig/modes.ts`. It writes the repository-keyed dual-mode record before command registration, supplies the resolved merge value/source to the persistent session projection, and is the only resolver any §1.4 recovery consumer may read; an unwritable run record refuses the Tier-1 run.

### 5.7 Run conduct

A run classifies what stopped it before acting: **clean** — nothing blocks; **soft** — attributable to the run's own last change and fixable without a new product decision; **hard** — outside existing authorization or requiring a non-substitutable human act. A clean state proceeds only to the resolved merge-mode ceiling. A soft blocker earns exactly one self-repair attempt; where §1.4's autonomous allowance and this budget reach one state, one intervention spends both rather than stacking attempts. A hard blocker emits one handoff record `{cause,recipient,reentry,observedAt,subjectHead,baseHead}` and stops. The record is idempotent on identical cause, recipient, route, and heads; it is an interruption fact, not a durable workflow state or label.

**Generation is open, decision is gated.** The shell may produce drafts, proposals, measurements, and candidate corrections, but every state transition stays behind its gate. Autonomous decision mode changes only the independent consumer at §5.6's closed three-checkpoint set. Trusted-account attribution, approval of an SSOT correction or genuinely new authorization, reversal of deliberate human state, disposal of another party's filed work, credentials, server configuration, another repository, and public or unretractable acts remain non-substitutable and hand off when reached. It never re-adjudicates an unchanged artifact.

**Human and administrative completeness.** No universal own-behalf or independent-identity restriction applies to Tier 2 or Tier 3. Native platform review semantics remain native; direct administrator operation is valid and outside Tier-1 guarantees. Tier-1 evidence still obeys §1.6.

#276 owns lifecycle transition writers and clearers; #278 owns the live mode resolver; §3.8 owns corrective `/land` migration. `/ship` remains review/closeout composition only, and human Tier 2 plus Tier 3 operation remains complete without either Tier-1 surface.

### 5.8 Context lifecycle

Working context is a managed resource, and the destructive reset is the last resort — narrowing what enters context (§1.5's bounded distillations, §2.8's budgeted surfaces) comes first. **A context discard is archive-then-discard, never delete**: before any discard, task-scoped state is distilled into at least one durable artifact, its field set defined by what a restore needs — the branch, the issue, the change under way, where the work stands, the next step. Reconstruction then reuses the one existing injection path rather than minting a parallel surface that can drift from it. Where the shell cannot intercept an outer discard mechanism, it front-loads the invariant: the archive step precedes the discard, and the trigger stays explicit — a wrong discard is irreversible within a session, exactly the cost shape that forbids automating it (§3.6).

Retrieval over durable memory is structurally bounded: a recall surface returns pointers whose worst-case cost is fixed and stated, never bodies — following a pointer is a separate, targeted read. The expensive deep tier is reachable only by explicit intent, with one bounded escalation permitted when the cheap tier misses on a substantive ask: the cheap miss already realized is the signal that justifies the spend. Cost-of-miss asymmetry governs affordances the way it governs faces (§3.6): a cheap recoverable miss earns an automatic nudge; an expensive one earns explicit-intent-only. Recurring advisories are rate-limited by design — an every-turn signal trains its reader to ignore it — and state read back from durable storage is validated at the boundary, never trusted as written (§3.9).

The norm is **explicitly advisory** (§3.1 rule 1): context economy is never a gate; the lifecycle instruments derive later per §1.2's macro-phase clause.

### 5.9 Session surfaces

Session-start work is time-boxed and staleness-stamped: an expensive check runs behind a time-to-live stamp, is wrapped in a timeout so a hung dependency never stalls startup, degrades to silence on error (§5.2's aid direction), and stamps only after a successful compute — a failed run must not debounce the next attempt. The recurring surface is one debounced, actionable line per degraded state, naming the state and its exact re-arm command (§5.2), kept alongside any per-invocation diagnostic floor — the once-per-session line is for the operator, the per-invocation line for the log reader, and neither replaces the other. A new measuring signal ships stating its own false-positive shapes and runs on demand until its precision is observed; only then does it earn an always-on surface — §3.6's measure step, applied to the measuring device itself. Check cadence derives from compute cost: a cheap presence check runs every session, while an expensive or privileged one stays occasional with its deferral named.

The disarm bar binds every surface: no enforcement-disabling state may be both reachable by one innocuous command and traceless — making a disarmed state observable is a separate, cheaper decision than changing its fail direction, so observability never waits on a posture debate. **The bar is discharged by an instrument, or by an enumerated residual whose recorded ground holds, and by nothing else.** A state placed outside it is recorded in place at the gate or tier that owns it, with the ground that put it there and with this bar named (§3.11's in-place rule) — so a reader who reaches a disarmable state from here can tell a violation from a settled exception by reading that gate's own record, and a state that is neither instrumented nor enumerated violates this bar however innocuous it looks. No instance list lives here: it would be a second enumeration drifting from the in-place ones, and the records point back to this bar precisely so no such list is needed. **What the bar ranges over is a STATE a clone can be in — never a gate's constant reach.** A state is something an act puts one clone into and leaves another without, and whose presence a reader cannot see from the gate's own text: a tracked path, an edited worktree file, an exported variable, a stale pointer. A gate that never evaluates some act evaluates it in no clone, is documented not to, and is therefore a SCOPE decision answerable at §3.3's rows — not a disarmed state, and not this bar's subject. The distinction is what keeps the bar decidable: read the other way, every uncovered act in the system would owe an observable, the bar would be unsatisfiable, and it would stop discriminating the case it exists for. It also settles the boundary that has been argued from both sides — a reach limit and a ref the ruleset does not cover are scope; an operator's edit to the very bytes a gate reads is a state. An act's own per-invocation spelling is scored with the persistent state it is a spelling of, never separately: a work tree named on the command line and one named in `core.worktree` are one state, and a flag that folds a tier is scored with the environment channels that fold it the same way. **And enumeration alone does not discharge the bar.** A residual discharges it where the record carries a ground and that ground holds; where a state is enumerated in place and no ground for it survives, the record says so and the state is a **declared deferral** — §3.6's terms, so it owes a decidable hardening trigger and a named owner for the hardened stage, and it is read as an open violation rather than as a settled exception. That third status is the one thing an author may not simply assert: writing the word buys nothing without the trigger and the owner beside it. And a detector mirrors the resolution order of the consumer it protects — reading the fallback exactly where the consumer would — or it is blind exactly where the consumer is live (§4.6's detector-placement rule is the structural limit case).

An operator-visible **act** is not a static tool noun. Its collapsed row exposes (1) the intent, (2) the structured target, and (3) a terminal class: success, failure, or refusal, with all three distinguishable. Refusal never borrows success styling or wording. Presentation cannot widen a channel: a publish row may name its requested destination but never the body, title, matched text, or raw result URL; a dispatch row may name the isolated-clone and blind-compare shapes but never the brief, delegate argv, expected ref, held object, or returned payload. The result renderer derives its class from the tool's existing disposition and error state; it neither invents nor changes a decision.

The minimal persistent projection uses the substrate's composable status slot rather than replacing its footer. It carries active-dispatch count, retaining the latest dispatch terminal class while idle, and #278's `.pi/extensions/gitjig/modes.ts` resolver feeds its resolved merge-mode value and source into the same composable status slot. No surface re-resolves one source or creates a rival authority. Current issue or PR and workflow phase are excluded because this runtime owns no authoritative value for either. Platform lifecycle labels and handoff records now have their owning #276 transition service, but remain excluded from this projection until #133 derives the persistent actor-neutral view; the projection may not infer authority from labels alone. Bind degradation stays on its owned, debounced actionable advisory above rather than being copied into a second state machine. A UI-less mode makes no status call; act decisions and automated progress never depend on rendering (§5.2, §4.4). Expanded act rows may expose an existing content-free refusal cause or unverified-outcome explanation, but never a payload the collapsed row withholds. During a dispatch only, the substrate's partial-result surface may render §4.9's bounded operator-only execution evidence; terminal rendering replaces it with the ordinary content-free act row, and headless execution retains no model-facing substitute. A real JSON-mode session arm, not a stubbed callback alone, proves that a distinctive delegate marker reaches `tool_execution_update` while occurring zero times in final result/details and the persisted session file; a renderer arm separately proves that the same content is exposed only when `isPartial` is true.

The norm is **explicitly advisory** (§3.1 rule 1). The first landed surface is the bind advisory (§3.2, §5.2), and it fixes one more rule for every successor: a detector reproduces the consumer's **resolution** and not the consumer's **execution** — the bind detector answers from the configuration git itself resolves and the layout the adapters derive from it, running no program of the repository it is classifying, because a classifier that executes what it classifies is no longer the read-only surface §5.2 places it in. Further surfaces derive per §1.2's macro-phase clause.

## 6. Self-governance milestone

This section states the criterion for the point at which this repository's own development runs under the shell it ships, and the standing posture each shell mechanism holds toward the substrate beneath it (§6.1).

The milestone is reached when both hold:

1. **Tier 1 self-applied** — the in-process gate for a class §3.3 homes at tier 1 loads from this repository's own tree in the sessions that develop this repository, blocking the norm violations it specifies here.
2. **Tier 2 self-bound** — this repository's development clones resolve `core.hooksPath` to their handed-over adapters (§3.2); an adopter's adapters invoke their handed-over `_lib.sh`/`helpers/` runtime, while the separately carried, pin-verified assets host tier 1 in that clone and this source repository resolves both tiers from its own tree.

Until then, an external development environment may govern the working process, under one absolute condition: it never surfaces in committed artifacts (§5.1). After the milestone, this repository is its own first adopter, and every norm in this SPEC is exercised on the shell's own development before any adopter meets it.

### 6.1 Substrate posture

The substrate under the shell is a rising floor: it improves under use and absorbs generic agent-support machinery over time. A shell mechanism that merely re-does what the substrate now does natively is redundant cost; the shell's durable value concentrates where a general substrate structurally cannot go — opinionated engineering policy, safety redundancy where §3.6's cost asymmetry calls for it, and repository artifacts as durable memory. Each shell mechanism therefore carries exactly one standing posture — **cede to the substrate**, **keep as policy**, or **keep as safety redundancy** — and a cede is a forward-discipline signal retired through its own change on the standard flow (§1.1), never an in-place deletion. §3.1 caps the classification: an enforcement-layer mechanism never resolves to cede on the strength of substrate-grown permissions — its floor posture is keep-as-safety-redundancy, because the only-safety-net commitment is substrate-evolution-proof by definition.

Tiers are capabilities, not universal installation stages: Tier 1 may be absent, Tier 2 may be unbound in a clone, and Tier 3 remains the repository floor. Parity and adopter classifiers therefore compare only the assets selected by the applicable capability profile; they never require every repository or clone to carry every tier. §3.8 Phases 4–7 own the configurable profile engine, surfaces, migration completion, and any separately authorized rollout.

Where this SPEC claims to classify a family exhaustively, a parity check fails until every member has its row; and an inventory this SPEC states is machine-checked against the real tree, or it rots — §2.4's clause that an exact count belongs where going stale fails a check, applied to trees. This SPEC also owes its own falsifiable acceptance checklist — observable, all-must-hold conditions read before the shell operates on a repository — committed to here and derived later like this section's parity and inventory checks. And build order follows consumption order — shared contracts before their consumers, templates before their readers, one end-to-end path proven before self-application (this section's milestone).

The norm is **explicitly advisory** (§3.1 rule 1): a design doctrine; the parity and inventory checks and the acceptance checklist derive later per §1.2's macro-phase clause.
